experimental_unit: one (trace, capacity) instance per variant, with N repeated wall-clock timing measurements per instance under the controlled campaign (median + variation reported, warm-up discarded -- see docs/practical_significance_ablation_protocol.md completion criteria).
comparison_design: within-instance: each optimized/selective/top-k/model-complexity variant is timed on the SAME (trace, capacity) instances as the canonical implementation; miss-ratio quality is compared against the already-certified fair-window baselines (analysis/reviewer_fairness/), never re-measured ad hoc.
reported_statistics: median and IQR wall-clock time per (trace, capacity, variant), warm-up repetitions discarded
speedup ratio (canonical median time / variant median time) per instance, with bootstrap 95% CI
component-level time breakdown (bookkeeping / candidate construction / feature extraction / model prediction / ranking / other) as a percentage of total, per instance
quality-cost tradeoff: miss_ratio vs. mean time-per-decision, per selective/top-k configuration
break-even miss-cost threshold vs. LRU/SIEVE/FIFO-Reinsertion and the strongest certified lightweight baseline

inferential_approach.primary_analysis: descriptive: median + bootstrap CI, not a significance test -- the practical-significance question is 'how large is the effect and is it worth the cost', not 'is there a nonzero effect' (timing differences at this scale are essentially always significant; magnitude and the break-even/Pareto framing are what matters)
inferential_approach.confidence_intervals: bootstrap (10,000 resamples over repetitions within each instance) 95% CI on median wall-clock time and on the speedup ratio
inferential_approach.reported_alongside_every_speedup_number: the underlying miss-ratio quality (never report a speedup without its quality cost/benefit in the same table)

explicit_prohibitions: Do not report a speedup number without its corresponding quality (miss-ratio) impact in the same table.
Do not select which variants/capacities to report after viewing controlled-campaign results (predeclared grid, matches the smoke-scale campaign already run and reported).

Do not run the controlled campaign, or this analysis, while any Concern 1/2/3 job or the legacy LRB is actively consuming CPU (see scripts/experiments/run_practical_significance_controlled.py's TIMING_GATE).
Report the honest 'no positive miss penalty makes the current policy preferable' outcome if that is what the break-even analysis shows -- do not hide or reframe a negative finding.
